about: The sheet for the Byrd Theatre cutaway: tools/cutaway/sheet.py. Callouts are anchored to drawn parts (history ids, in the isometric view and the flat section); each callout gives its badge's confidence. Callout text is a working draft, written with Claude, for the artist to edit. The holly border and the red and green of the title and headings are sheet decoration, not part of the drawing.
title: The Byrd Theatre, Christmas Eve 1928
subtitle: Opening night, cut down the middle from the Cary Street doors to the screen
sectionCaption: The same cut, seen flat: Cary Street on the left, the stage and the organ on the right

groups.title: From the sidewalk to a seat

callouts.title: West Cary Street
callouts.text: Red brick and white terra cotta, a black marble box office, and a plain bronze marquee with no lettering. The corner sign is drawn without its letters.

callouts.title: Two sets of doors
callouts.text: An outer lobby between two sets of a dozen brass-framed glass doors (28 doors, by a 1986 count).

callouts.title: The lobby
callouts.text: A vaulted, gold-leafed ceiling twenty-five feet up, marble halfway up the walls, and a mezzanine lounge on three sides. Its plan is approximate.

callouts.title: Pool and fountain
callouts.text: Twenty feet by eight, with a fountain and fish; a candy stand replaced it about 1940. Its place is approximate.

callouts.title: Orchestra
callouts.text: 916 seats today, 19 inches wide, in red velvet. The rows and aisles of 1928 are not recorded.

callouts.title: Balcony
callouts.text: 476 seats today. Its depth and rake are approximate.

callouts.title: Segregated
callouts.text: The Byrd was segregated: Black patrons were not admitted until the 1960s. Where seats were set apart is not known; none are drawn.

callouts.title: Dome and chandelier
callouts.text: Four thousand crystals and three hundred bulbs in four colors, some two tons, lowered for relamping.

callouts.title: Murals
callouts.text: Six in niches high on the side walls and more behind the boxes, by Arthur Brounet. The paintings are not drawn.

callouts.title: Projection booth
callouts.text: Two Simplex projectors, Vitaphone sound, and the switchboard for every light, the curtain and the masking. Its place is approximate.

callouts.title: Air tunnels
callouts.text: Three concrete tunnels under the floor carried the cooled air. Their routes are not known.

callouts.title: Gold grille
callouts.text: Along the whole proscenium, hiding the openings of the organ chambers.

callouts.title: Organ chambers
callouts.text: Opus 1948, four manuals and seventeen ranks, in two rooms over the stage, with a room for the relays. Their layout is approximate.

callouts.title: The console
callouts.text: Mahogany, on its own lift from the open pit. On opening night Carl Rhond played, with Velma Beck and Winston Neville; the program was a film and the organ.

callouts.title: Piano and harp
callouts.text: In the boxes either side of the stage, played from the console. Which held which is not known.

sources: Sources: National Register nomination, Byrd Theatre (Virginia DHR 127-0287, 1977–79), with its USGS map; Miles J. Rudisill Jr., Theatre Organ, Jan.–Feb. 1986, and its 1928 photographs; Byrd Theatre Foundation (About; Theatre History; The Mighty Wurlitzer Organ; balcony seats, Jan. 2025); Wikipedia, Byrd Theatre, for today's seat counts and, citing the Richmond Times-Dispatch (April 8, 2002), segregation; the front c. 1929 (RVA Rephotography Project); OpenStreetMap contributors (the street, the outlines); USGS 3DEP lidar (the ground); City of Richmond, year of construction (the neighbors); National Weather Service, Richmond Christmas Day records; Museum District Association.
notes: No plan, section or seating chart of the building was found. Rooms are placed from written descriptions and photographs inside the 84 x 135 ft lot of the nomination; only the lot and the lobby's height are given in feet. Sources differ: 1,396 seats (the nomination, used here), 1,390 (1986), 1,392 (Wikipedia), 1,200 (the foundation today); 4,000 crystals and two tons (the nomination) or 5,000 and two and a half tons (the foundation); three organ chambers (the nomination), two and a relay room (the foundation), or four rooms. The cut runs 5 ft east of the center line, so the chandelier and the console stand whole. West Cary Street, its sidewalks and the ground are today's (OpenStreetMap; USGS 3DEP lidar), and the model is set on the theatre's OpenStreetMap outline, which measures within 0.2 m of the lot. A neighbor is drawn only where the city assessor's year built puts it up by 1928: the one-storey shops to the west (1923), which the c. 1929 photograph also shows. The building next door to the east is dated 1929 and is not drawn; the houses and the corner building beyond it stand on the side lifted away and are left out. No snow: the Weather Service records none on the ground in Richmond on Christmas Day 1928. No decorations are drawn in the building, since no account of any was found. The holly and the red and green of the title and headings are the sheet's own decoration.
